edges.relation: The bit-tree is the search structure; descent pruning is the primary elimination rule applied at each node
Path-merging is a secondary pruning rule applied during bit-tree traversal when descent fails
OEE is a tertiary pruning rule applied during bit-tree traversal, checking symbolic step patterns
Survivors of the bit-tree are passed to the bitvector stage for further sieving of the top A bits
The mod-9 sieve is incorporated into the bitvector via bitwise AND, combining two filters in one operation
Bitvectors are stored in GPU shared memory; warp-uniform dispatch ensures efficient access patterns
The rational approximation 485/306 provides the exact integer criterion that makes descent pruning rigorous
The dip_B values in bitvectors are computed using the 485/306 approximation to determine descent thresholds
Individual GPU kernels process work units; distributed sharding assigns work units across multiple GPUs
GPU Step 3 iteration can use either LUT-based acceleration or run-length approaches, trading cache for computation
Information-directed ordering replaces DFS in the bit-tree to optimize CPU-GPU pipeline overlap
The information gain of a branch depends on the density of its corresponding bitvector BV_i
The adaptive scaling property determines optimal recursion depth N-A based on the survival rate S(N)
As N grows and S(N) shrinks, work units become smaller, affecting load balance across distributed workers
Both exploit the preimage structure of the Collatz map — mod-9 detects T-preimages, path-merging detects T^k-preimages
Both detect trajectory merges but via different mechanisms: OEE uses step-pattern automata, path-merging uses mod-3 residues
The LUT stores 3^f values that directly feed into the 485f <= 306k descent criterion

bridge_chains.name: number_theory_to_GPU_pipeline
bridge_chains.description: Transforms a number-theoretic descent criterion into an integer inequality, encodes it in compressed bitvectors, and dispatches to GPU with uniform workloads. Crosses: optimization_theory -> numerical_analysis -> data_compression -> GPU_computing.

bridge_chains.name: tree_search_to_distributed_computation
bridge_chains.description: Explores the Collatz search space as a binary tree, orders exploration by information gain, dispatches to GPUs, and distributes across supercomputer clusters. Crosses: tree_search -> information_theory -> GPU_computing -> distributed_computing.

bridge_chains.name: automata_to_compression
bridge_chains.description: Detects trajectory patterns via finite automata, identifies path merges via modular arithmetic, filters by residue classes, and compresses all checks into bitwise AND operations. Crosses: automata_theory -> compiler_optimization -> number_theory -> data_compression.

bridge_chains.name: probability_to_architecture
bridge_chains.description: Uses probabilistic analysis of survival rates to set algorithm parameters, which determine recursion depth, lookup table sizes, and GPU dispatch granularity. Crosses: probability_theory -> tree_search -> dynamic_programming -> GPU_computing.

bridge_chains.name: dynamical_systems_to_fault_tolerance
bridge_chains.description: The concentration-of-measure property of Collatz dynamics (fewer survivors at higher N) directly impacts work-unit sizing and fault-tolerance strategies in distributed verification. Crosses: dynamical_systems -> distributed_computing.
